name: dunnie (doonie)

attributes.attribute: Northumbrian sprite that disguised itself as a midwife's horse
Scottish form of the same horse-shaped sprite

sources: Spence, Lewis. The Minor Traditions of British Mythology. (New York: Benjamin Blom, Inc., 1972), 92.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The dunnie was a mischievous Northumbrian sprite. During a woman's labor it disguised itself as the midwife's horse. It then disappeared, leaving the midwife stranded. It played the same trick on ploughmen who went to harness the team in a barn. In Scotland the same creature took the name doonie. It often appeared in the shape of a horse. It could also seem to be an old woman or a man. The doonie shared the wicked and sometimes dangerous teasing of its southern relative.
